name: Alex Wang
milestone_by_age_26: In 2016, at age 19, dropped out of MIT and co-founded Scale AI with Lucy Guo (Y Combinator) to provide data labeling and evaluation infrastructure for machine learning—launching what became a multi-billion-dollar AI data platform.
early_history_summary: Born January 1997 in Los Alamos, New Mexico, to Chinese immigrant physicists at Los Alamos National Laboratory. Excelled in math/CS competitions (USACO finalist; Math Olympiad Program 2013; U.S. Physics Team 2014), worked as a teen engineer at Addepar and Quora, briefly attended MIT and interned at Hudson River Trading, then left school to found Scale AI.
family_context_summary: Son of Chinese immigrants who worked as physicists at Los Alamos National Laboratory; raised in a high-education science community in New Mexico.
parent_family_domain_summary: Both parents were physicists at a national lab, providing strong STEM fluency and academic norms adjacent to quantitative/technical careers, though not directly AI entrepreneurship.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Math/physics olympiads, USACO, physicist parents, Los Alamos, MIT/YC, teen engineering jobs, AI data wave
evidence_summary: Wang’s age-19 founding of Scale AI is multiply sourced (Wikipedia, Forbes, Business Insider). Pre-founding olympiad credentials and teen SWE roles show serious early reps. Parent STEM platform and later YC/SV network accelerated growth; by 2021 he was among the youngest self-made billionaires via Scale’s valuation, later becoming Meta’s Chief AI Officer after Meta’s 2025 Scale investment.
starting_point: Born January 1997 in Los Alamos, New Mexico, to Chinese immigrant parents who worked as physicists at Los Alamos National Laboratory.
current_position: Chief AI Officer at Meta Platforms and founder/board member of Scale AI after Meta’s ~$14.3B investment; former Scale CEO and among the youngest self-made tech billionaires.

trajectory.event: Qualified for the Math Olympiad Program; also a multi-year USACO finalist during high school.
Named to the U.S. Physics Team while at Los Alamos High School.
Dropped out of MIT and co-founded Scale AI with Lucy Guo; entered Y Combinator to build AI data-labeling infrastructure.
Named to Forbes 30 Under 30 in Enterprise Technology as Scale grew enterprise ML customers.
Scale’s valuation surge made Wang one of the world’s youngest self-made billionaires on paper.
Meta invested ~$14.3B for a large Scale stake; Wang stepped down as Scale CEO to become Meta’s Chief AI Officer leading Superintelligence Labs.

milestone_by_age_26: In 2005, at about age 23, co-created Stanford’s Stanley autonomous vehicle team that won the DARPA Grand Challenge; self-supervised vision/terrain work was central, later recognized with a Stanford AI Lab gold medal and Smithsonian display of Stanley.

Key contributor on Stanley’s winning 2005 DARPA Grand Challenge stack; later co-founded and served as CEO of Udacity and co-founded medical AI company Nines.
family_context_summary: Raised in Sioux City, Iowa; further family financial/parental domain details not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Princeton at 19, Stanford AI Lab, Sebastian Thrun, DARPA Grand Challenge team, self-driving research wave
evidence_summary: Birth year 1982 and DARPA 2005 co-creator role are supported by Wikipedia plus team publications and Stanford recognition. Early Princeton graduation shows prior intensity; Thrun mentorship and Stanford team multiplied scarce autonomy skills at the exact DARPA structural opening. Later Udacity CEO path compounds operator impact but the ≤26 qualifying event is Stanley/DARPA.
starting_point: Born 1982 and raised in Sioux City, Iowa; early academic acceleration led to a Princeton CS degree at age 19 before Stanford graduate work.
current_position: Entrepreneur and advisor (including Future Family); co-founder of Udacity and Nines; known for foundational work on Stanford’s Stanley self-driving team that fed into Waymo’s origins.

trajectory.event: Graduated Princeton with a B.S.E. in Computer Science, magna cum laude, at age 19.
Co-created Stanford’s Stanley team that won the DARPA Grand Challenge using self-supervised road/terrain learning.
Won Qualcomm Innovation Fellowship with Jesse Levinson for indoor WiFi localization research at Stanford.
Completed Stanford Ph.D. under Sebastian Thrun and co-founded Udacity, serving as founding CEO.
Udacity reached ~$1B valuation after major growth-capital rounds.
Co-founded Nines, building AI-enabled, FDA-cleared teleradiology tools.
